title: Booking a study room at the library

lines.t: Good morning. University Library, information desk.
Hello. I would like to book a study room for a group project, please.
Of course. How many students will there be?
Five of us. We need a room for about three hours.
Let me see. The small rooms take four people, so you will need a large room. Those have a screen and a whiteboard.
That would be perfect. Is anything free on Tuesday?
On Tuesday, there is a room free from ten until twelve, and again from three until six.
Could we have the afternoon one? We have classes in the morning.
Yes. But the maximum booking is two hours at a time, so I can give you three until five.
That is fine. Is there a way to extend it if no one else needs the room?
Yes. Come to the desk before five, and we will check. Can I have a name and a student number?
Ahmed Saidi, S, A, I, D, I. My number is two zero two three, four four one.
Thank you, Ahmed. It is Room Nine on the second floor. Please remember that you can't eat in the rooms, but you can bring water.
Understood. Thank you very much.

qs.q: The group has ___ students.
Why can't they use a small room?
Which day do they book?
What time is the booking?
qs.why: الحد الأقصى ساعتان فيحجزون من الثالثة إلى الخامسة.

qs.q: They have Room ___ on the second floor.
Students can bring water into the rooms.
They must speak to the desk before the booking ends to extend it.
qs.why: عليه الحضور إلى المكتب قبل الخامسة.

lines.t: Welcome to the City Science Museum audio guide. Please press the green button when you want to hear the next section.
You are now standing in the Hall of Inventions. Straight ahead, you can see a large glass case.
Inside is a copy of the first mechanical clock made in this region, around the year thirteen hundred.
Notice how big it is. The clockmaker used heavy weights and a system of wheels, and the clock only showed the hour.
It did not have a minute hand.
On your left, there is a model of an early printing machine. Before this invention, people copied books by hand, and a single book could take months.
With the machine, a workshop could print hundreds of pages in a day, and knowledge spread faster than ever before.
Please do not touch the models, but children can try the interactive screens near the window. They show how the machine worked.
When you are ready, go through the blue door at the end of the hall to the Energy Gallery. The audio guide will start automatically.
The cafe is on the ground floor, and the museum closes at five thirty.

qs.q: What should visitors press to hear the next section?
What is inside the large glass case?
o: A copy of an early clock

qs.q: The old clock had a minute hand.
Where is the model of the printing machine?

qs.why: نسخ كتاب واحد قد يستغرق شهوراً.

title: An interview with a young lawyer

lines.t: Today, I am talking to Samira, a young lawyer who works for a legal aid centre. Samira, why did you choose law?
When I was fifteen, my uncle lost his job unfairly, and nobody explained his rights to him.
I decided then that I wanted to help people understand the law.
What does a normal day look like?
There is no normal day, really. In the morning, I usually meet clients who cannot afford a private lawyer.
Many of them have problems with rent, work contracts or family issues.
Is it a stressful job?
Sometimes, yes. There is a lot of paperwork, and some cases take months. But when a family keeps their home because of my work, it is very rewarding.
What skills are most important?
Listening, first of all. People often need to tell their story before you can help them. Then, clear writing, because a letter to a court must be precise.
Do you use technology?
More and more. We use software to find old cases quickly, which saves hours every week.
What is your advice for law students?
Do an internship during your studies. You learn more in one month in a real office than in a whole semester of reading.
Thank you, Samira.

qs.q: Why did Samira decide to study law?
o: Her uncle lost his job unfairly

qs.q: Who are Samira's clients?
o: People who cannot afford a private lawyer
qs.why: عملاؤها لا يستطيعون دفع أتعاب محامٍ خاص.

qs.q: Her job is never stressful.
She says the most important skill is ___.
How does software help the centre?
Her advice is to do an ___ during your studies.
Samira says reading for a semester teaches more than a month in an office.

lines.t: Hello and welcome to Smart Student, the podcast about making life easier on a small budget.
I am your host, and today I have four simple ideas for saving money.
The first idea is to track your spending. For one month, write down everything you buy, even a small coffee.
Most people are surprised to find that these little purchases add up to about thirty or forty pounds a month.
The second idea is to plan your meals.
When you cook at home and carry your lunch, you can easily save fifty pounds a month compared with eating out.
Third, use your student card. Many shops, cinemas and train companies give discounts of ten to twenty percent, but a lot of students forget to ask.
My fourth idea is to save first, and spend later. On the day you receive your money, move a small amount, perhaps ten percent, to a separate account.
If you don't see it, you won't spend it.
Remember, you don't have to change your life in one day. Start with one idea this week, and add another next month.
That is all for today. Next time, we will talk about buying second-hand books. Goodbye!

qs.q: The host has ___ ideas for saving money.
What should listeners write down?
Small purchases can add up to about 30 or ___ pounds a month.
How much can cooking at home save?

What should you do on the day you receive money?
o: Move a small amount to another account
qs.why: حوّل مبلغاً صغيراً إلى حساب منفصل.

title: Complaining politely about an internet connection

lines.t: Customer service, Mark speaking. How can I help you?
Hello, Mark. I am calling about my internet connection. I am afraid it has been very slow for the last two weeks.
I am sorry to hear that. Can I have your account number?
Yes, it is four eight one, nine two six.
Thank you. Let me look. Which package do you have?
The fifty megabit package. But in the evening, I can hardly watch a video, and my online classes keep stopping.
I see. Have you tried restarting the router?
Yes, I turned it off for a minute several times, and I also moved it into the living room. It didn't help.
Okay. I can see some problems on your line. I will send an engineer to check it.
When could he come? I am at university in the daytime.
We have a free slot on Thursday between five and seven in the evening.
That works for me. Will I have to pay for the visit?
No, it is free, because the fault is on our side. And I will give you a ten dollar credit on your next bill.
Thank you. I appreciate your help.

qs.q: How long has the connection been slow?
The customer has the ___ megabit package.
What problem does he have in the evening?
qs.why: لا يستطيع مشاهدة فيديو والدروس تتوقف.

qs.q: He moved the router to the living room.
qs.why: قال إنه نقله إلى غرفة المعيشة.

qs.q: When can the engineer come?
The customer must pay for the engineer's visit.
qs.why: الزيارة مجانية لأن العطل من جهة الشركة.

title: A short lecture: how the internet works

lines.t: Good morning. Today, I would like to give you a simple picture of how the internet works.
First, the internet is not one machine.
It is a huge network of millions of computers, phones and servers that are connected with each other by cables, wireless signals and satellites.
Most of the data, about ninety-five percent, travels through cables under the sea.
When you open a web page, your computer sends a request. Think of it as a letter with an address.
This address is called an IP address, and every device has one.
The request does not travel in one piece. Instead, it is cut into small packets.
Each packet can take a different route, like cars choosing different roads to the same city.
At the end, your computer puts the packets back in the correct order.
Servers are computers that store web pages and send them to you when you ask.
Large companies keep thousands of servers in big buildings called data centres, which need a lot of electricity and cooling.
Finally, a word about names. People remember words, not numbers, so a system called the domain name system works like a phone book.
It changes a name like a university website into the correct IP address.
Next week, we will discuss internet security.

qs.q: What is the internet, according to the lecturer?
o: A network of many connected devices
qs.why: شبكة ضخمة من أجهزة كثيرة متصلة.

qs.q: About ___ percent of data travels through undersea cables.
What does an IP address resemble?
A request travels as one big piece.
What do data centres need a lot of?

What is next week's topic?
